fromObservable Behavior

fromObservable is a FeatureCell API extension that converts an Observable<T> into a normalized StateType<T>, allowing asynchronous observable results to be injected into the pipeline using standard state update APIs.

This behavior operates outside of the pipeline and does not participate directly in Resolve, operator, filter, or reducer stages. Instead, it acts as a bridge that resolves a single observable emission and produces a structured state envelope suitable for pipeline admission.

fromObservable exists primarily as a migration and interoperability aid for engineers accustomed to Redux-style patterns, where state updates are often wrapped in observables and manually normalized before dispatch. It enables those workflows to transition cleanly into the SDuX model without requiring immediate changes to application architecture.

This behavior extends the FeatureCell instance by adding a fromObservable() method that returns an Observable<StateType<T>>. The returned observable may then be passed directly to replaceState or mergeState.

When fromObservable() is invoked, the source observable is subscribed once. The first emitted value is wrapped in a standard state envelope and emitted downstream, after which the subscription completes. Errors are normalized into pipeline-compatible error objects.

Subscription lifetime is bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle. Active subscriptions are automatically terminated on reset or destruction, ensuring that observable resolution cannot outlive the owning FeatureCell or produce orphaned state updates.

Note

fromObservable() is a single-resolution bridge, not a streaming mechanism. It exists primarily to support migration from Redux-style or externally managed async flows where observables are resolved before state submission.

In most cases, it is recommended to pass the observable directly to replaceState or mergeState and allow the Resolve stage to handle normalization automatically. This reduces indirection, minimizes unnecessary wrapping code, and avoids subtle debugging issues caused by resolving values outside the pipeline.

Use fromObservable() only when you explicitly need to adapt or transform an observable into a StateType<T> envelope before submission. For continuous or high-frequency observable sources that emit over time, use fromStream() instead.

Diagram
Configuration

withCoreFromObservableBehavior is configured by invoking the fromObservable() method on an initialized FeatureCell. This method wraps an observable source and returns a derived observable that emits normalized StateType<T> values.

Unlike resolve behaviors that execute inside the pipeline, withCoreFromObservableBehavior operates outside of pipeline execution. It acts as a bridge that converts observable emissions into standard state envelopes, which can then be injected into the pipeline using replaceState or mergeState.

The observable produced by fromObservable() emits at most a single normalized state value and completes. Subscription lifetime is automatically bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle and is terminated on reset or destruction, ensuring that asynchronous resolution cannot outlive the owning cell.

This API exists primarily as a migration and interoperability bridge for patterns common in Redux-style systems, where asynchronous sources are resolved externally and then dispatched as state updates. In most cases, directly supplying observables to the vault and allowing the Resolve stage to handle normalization is preferred.

FeatureCell Observable Integration

withCoreFromObservableBehavior extends the FeatureCell instance with a fromObservable() method, providing a bridge for integrating RxJS observables into state updates without directly submitting the observable to the pipeline.

Unlike replaceState and mergeState, which accept finalized state inputs, fromObservable() wraps an observable source and produces a derived observable that emits a normalized StateType<T> value.

This method does not inject values into the pipeline automatically. Instead, it externalizes observable resolution and allows the resulting state envelope to be explicitly submitted using replaceState or mergeState. Resolution and commitment still occur through the standard Resolve and State stages.

Extended FeatureCell API
API Description

.fromObservable(source$)

inputs:

  • source$: Observable<T>

returns:

  • Observable<StateType<T>>

Wraps an observable source and resolves a single emitted value into a normalized state envelope containing value, loading, and error fields.

The returned observable completes after emitting once and is automatically bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle. Subscriptions are terminated on reset or destruction, preventing asynchronous resolution from outliving the owning cell.

This API is intended as a migration and interoperability bridge for Redux-style or external async flows, where values are traditionally resolved outside the store and then dispatched as state updates.

Examples

withCoreFromObservableBehavior provides a bridge for resolving a single value from an Observable and converting it into a normalized StateType.

Unlike fromStream(), which continuously injects values, fromObservable() resolves exactly once. The resulting state envelope must then be explicitly injected into the pipeline using mergeState or replaceState.

In the examples below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, an observable is resolved using fromObservable(), and the resulting state envelope is forwarded into the pipeline using mergeState.

Example 1: Resolve an Observable and Inject the Result

{{`@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();

    // Observable defined locally in the cell
    const employees$ = of([
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ]);

    // Resolve the observable once and inject the result into the pipeline
    this.vault.fromObservable(employees$).subscribe({
      next: (incoming: StateType<Employee[]>) => this.vault.mergeState(incoming)
    });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`import { of } from 'rxjs';

export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

// Observable defined locally in the module
const employees$ = of([
  { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
]);

// Resolve the observable once and inject the result into the pipeline
employeeCell.fromObservable(employees$).subscribe({
  next: (incoming: StateType<Employee[]>) => this.vault.mergeState(incoming)
});`}}
